title: SDK wrap satisfies the execute liveness budget
statement: The client's wrapForExecute produces a transaction that meets the on-chain execute liveness budget: ComputeBudget instructions are hoisted TOP-LEVEL; the SetComputeUnitLimit is strictly decoded and validated against a measured floor and Solana's ceiling; a RequestHeapFrame is ALWAYS attached, sized from the real heap drivers (inner-instruction count, account references, payload bytes) and clamped to [128 KiB floor, 256 KiB ceiling] as a multiple of 1024, and a caller-supplied frame is preserved ONLY if it clears the runtime's alignment + range rules and covers the shape; and the on-chain account caps are enforced client-side from the effective post-coalescing privileges so an over-cap shape fails fast.

evidence.name: always attaches a RequestHeapFrame at or above the measured floor
keeps a dApp price setting AND still injects a validated compute-unit limit
rejects a dApp compute-unit limit below the measured floor
rejects a configured default limit below the floor
validates a caller-supplied heap frame against the runtime range and alignment
counts a payer-promoted remaining account against the writable cap
rejects a shape past the on-chain account cap

notes: WRDF-0072 (r1+r2): the frame is sized by inner-instruction count (255 empty ixs OOM at remainingLen==1). WRDF-0076: the CU limit is decoded and floored at ~113k handler cost (120k). WRDF-0077: caps count effective post-coalescing writability. WRDF-0080: a caller-supplied frame is validated against Agave's MIN/MAX + 1024-alignment before being kept, else rejected — a misaligned or over-ceiling frame would revert the tx on-chain.

title: Generic execute never signs for a foreign token account the vault is delegate of
statement: On both the session and root `execute` paths, before any CPI, the handler rejects (err 6078 VaultDelegatedForeignAccountInPayload) any account in the logical list — the signer slot (logical 1) included, not only `remaining_accounts` — that is a token account whose owner is not the vault PDA and whose account-level `delegate` is the vault PDA, regardless of `delegated_amount`; a foreign token account delegated to any other pubkey is unaffected.
code_ref: programs/warden/src/conservation/compare.rs (reject_vault_delegated_foreign_accounts) + programs/warden/src/instructions/execute.rs (call sites after the WRDF-0105 mint gate, before the registry check: once over `before`, once over the signer-slot snapshot)
notes: Fable audit P-1 (docs/security/FABLE-AUDIT-2026-09-02.md). RED was run against the SHIPPED .so (LiteSVM loads target/deploy/warden.so; the first GREEN attempt silently tested the stale binary until `anchor build --features test-jup` was rerun -- a harness footgun worth remembering): both `_rejected` tests reported "expected reject with custom 6078, got success" with 9,000 of a stranger's tokens transferred (session) / burned (root) at zero recorded outflow and no bucket debit. The rule is BEFORE-snapshot ONLY, deliberately: an AFTER re-application was implemented and its test could not be made to fail because SPL Token clears `delegate` when `delegated_amount` reaches zero -- exactly the full-drain shape leaves no delegate to observe -- so the after-check was dropped as void rather than kept as decoration (recorded in the rule's doc comment so nobody re-adds it in good faith). A delegation can only be CREATED mid-payload by the logical-1 submitter Approve-ing its own account, which the submitter could do directly anyway; that shape is out of scope for this row. `delegated_amount` is deliberately not consulted: a delegate with 0 remaining is still an anomaly the vault has no business being in. Narrowness control: a stranger account delegated to a third pubkey rides read-only beside an honest transfer. Relation to WRDF-0105: that finding closed the MINT-level roles the PDA can hold; this row is the ACCOUNT-level sibling (WRDF-0111: the relation used to sit in `prior_art`, which is reserved for corpus IDs). Codex sol@max round over 3766e24 (thread 06aac9dfd711-20260902T044843Z) re-raised the rule as WRDF-0109: it ran over `before`, which is positional over `remaining_accounts` only, so logical 1 — the `Signer`, an arbitrary keypair address of which Anchor checks only `is_signer` — was never examined; a submitter whose own address was the delegated account passed it WRITABLE at slot 1 and drained it on both paths (RED at 0757d7d, 9,000 moved, no bucket debit). Fixed at 2ddf781: the signer slot is snapshotted once and fed through every pre-CPI gate `before` goes through (unsupported writable owners, both WRDF-0105 mint gates, this rule); it stays out of the positional conservation pair. Logical 0 is the SmartAccount PDA, program-owned by construction. Sibling authority shape: WRD-EXEC-14 (multisig).

title: Generic execute never signs for a token-program Multisig the vault is a member of
statement: On both the session and root `execute` paths, before any CPI AND again after the last CPI (before conservation), the handler rejects (err 6079 VaultMultisigMemberInPayload) any account in the logical list — the signer slot included — that is an SPL Token or Token-2022 `Multisig` (exactly 355 bytes, owned by either token program, initialized) naming the vault PDA among its live `signers[..n]`, whether or not the payload references it and whether it existed before the payload ran or was created by it; a multisig whose live members are all other pubkeys is unaffected, and a key sitting in a slot at or past `n` is not a member.
code_ref: programs/warden/src/conservation/compare.rs (multisig_names_member, reject_vault_multisig_members) + programs/warden/src/instructions/execute.rs (two call sites over logical[1..]: beside the BEFORE snapshot, and beside the AFTER snapshot)
notes: Codex WRDF-0110 (sol@max round over the P-1 fix, thread 06aac9dfd711-20260902T044843Z). The THIRD authority shape the PDA can satisfy, after the five mint-level roles (WRDF-0105, err 6076) and the account-level delegate (WRD-EXEC-13, err 6078): the token program accepts a Multisig as the owner/delegate/close/mint/freeze authority of anything, satisfied by `m` member signatures, and the forwarded PDA signature is one. A stranger makes a 1-of-1 multisig with the vault as member, owns a token account by it, and `Transfer(source, dest, authority = M, signers = [PDA])` moves the tokens: conservation skips the non-vault-owned source, and a 355-byte account is deliberately classified as neither mint nor token account (`snapshot::classify`), its `token_parse_failed` fatal only for accounts that were vault-owned before. RED at 0757d7d against the shipped .so: "expected reject with custom 6079, got success", 9,000 moved. The predicate is a pure byte function on (owner_program, data) rather than a new `Snap` field, so the heap-bound execute path runs it over every logical account without allocating and `snapshot_one` keeps its signature; it walks exactly `signers[..min(n, 11)]` as `validate_owner` does, and an uninitialized multisig is not an authority to the token program either. BEFORE and AFTER, unlike its siblings, and the AFTER pass is load-bearing: while writing this row the BEFORE-only rule at 2ddf781 was bypassed by CREATING the multisig inside the payload — the submitter's keypair address (logical 1, writable signer, pre-funded with rent) is a plain System account when the BEFORE gate runs; `Allocate(355)` + `Assign(token program)` + `InitializeMultisig2(M, [PDA])` + `Transfer(authority = M, signers = [PDA])` drained a stranger's M-owned account (RED at 2ddf781, "got success", 9,000 moved). The delegate rule's AFTER pass was proven VOID because the token program clears a spent delegate; the token program never erases a multisig, so the AFTER state always shows one. Closed at 14ee34b. Codex round 2 over 2ddf781..14ee34b OWED at the time of this row. ROUND 2 (over the fixes 2ddf78139b84a3d2abf2cc005cc31cc5e3b1aba1 + 14ee34b7daa4f58c2b4e49c123ff11e58393fdcd) COULD NOT BE RECORDED on 2026-09-02: scripts/review.sh (gpt-5.6-sol@max) was refused twice by the OpenAI cyber content filter on the drain-proving regressions in this range, and scripts/review-grok.sh produced two artefacts the anti-silence validator correctly rejected. The fix range therefore has NO recorded adversarial review; it is still OWED and is round R0 in docs/CODEX-HANDOVER-2026-09-02.md. The remediation_verified flips on WRDF-0109/0110/0111 certify only that the fixes are in and the FULL gate ran green at e8365a76b43779cf4bd8032603a1f6bfcfca8831, not that a reviewer confirmed them.

title: Execute conservation includes the transaction signer slot
statement: On both root and session `execute`, the positional BEFORE/AFTER conservation set is every logical account except logical[0] (the Anchor-validated SmartAccount), including logical[1] even though it is also the transaction signer; if that address is a vault-owned token account, its net outflow is coalesced, checked against the applicable root/session limits, and debited from the shared account bucket, with session lifetime spend also debited on the session path.
notes: WRDF-0115. The finding refuted the historical final sentence in WRD-CAP-01/09 claiming their evidence had never been wrong for vault-owned balances, and supersedes WRD-EXEC-13's historical remediation note saying logical[1] stays out of conservation. At 2ddf781 both focused tests were RED: each token transfer succeeded while the expected 9,000-unit debit remained zero. At 37c0435 both are GREEN, and the full execute test binary is 71 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored. The key distinction is that transaction-signature authority belongs to an account address, while SPL token ownership is a field in that account's data; one does not preclude the other. Full repository-gate verification is pending.

title: Generic execute never signs as close authority for a foreign token account
statement: On both root and session `execute`, before any CPI, the handler rejects (err 6080 VaultCloseAuthorityForeignAccountInPayload) every classic SPL Token or Token-2022 account in the complete logical snapshot except the Anchor-validated SmartAccount whose token owner is not the vault PDA and whose account-level close_authority is the vault PDA; this includes logical[1] even when it is the transaction signer, while a foreign account naming another close authority is unaffected.
notes: WRDF-0119. SPL Token authorizes CloseAccount with close_authority.unwrap_or(owner), so this role is independent of the foreign-delegate rule in WRD-EXEC-13. Direct closes are deny-scanned, but a root forwarding CPI can hide the token opcode. RED at 18a20c4f5cbbd7f156d28da24b6c1ada9dcb9b5e: after rebuilding the shipped SBF, `cargo test --locked -p warden --features test-jup --test execute codex_wrdf0119 -- --nocapture` reported the root classic-SPL nested close and session Token-2022 signer-slot cases both succeeded when err 6080 was expected; the stranger-close-authority control passed. GREEN over the fix at a5ca4b57aa0a34c1a62a54a0f2d4633c77706ea0: the same command passed 3/3. BEFORE-only is intentional because a successful close removes its authority field; assigning the role mid-payload requires the foreign token owner to sign. Full repository-gate verification is pending.

title: `frozen` gates every 1A outflow and every grant
statement: While SmartAccount.frozen is set, no Phase 1A instruction that moves value or widens authority succeeds: `transfer` on both the session and the root path, and `grant_session`.
notes: SCOPED TO THE 1A SURFACES DELIBERATELY. `execute`, `swap` and `execute_pending` are covered by WRD-FRZ-03 at `unimplemented`; naming them here would have let 1A tests stand as evidence for instructions that do not exist. A frozen-gate negative test is on the acceptance checklist for each of them.

title: A freeze is not a brick
statement: rotate_nonce still succeeds while frozen, so the root can always prove liveness and reach unfreeze; freeze blocks value movement, not the root ceremony itself.
notes: The 1A unfreeze timelock is read LIVE from policy.timelock_secs at lift time. 1B's set_policy must make a deliberate choice for an already-frozen account: preserve the live read, or snapshot at freeze time. That decision opens a new invariant when it lands.

title: 1B value paths refuse while frozen
statement: execute, swap and execute_pending each refuse while frozen, re-validated against CURRENT state at execution rather than at queue time.
notes: execute_pending is permissionless after execute_after, so the frozen check is the only thing standing between a queued action and a freeze that landed after it was queued. B4 (2026-08-23): DELIBERATELY NOT PROMOTED. The statement is a conjunction over execute, swap and execute_pending; `execute_pending` does not exist in the program (Phase 1C), so no evidence can satisfy the row. Both built paths are enforced (execute.rs / swap.rs refuse on current state before authorization) and are now BOTH tested — execute_frozen_rejected plus the new swap_frozen_rejected, which closes a real hole (swap had no frozen test at all). To promote in 1C you additionally need an execute_pending-while-frozen test where the freeze lands AFTER queueing, which is the point of this row.

title: Proof of possession at account creation
statement: create_account cannot succeed without a valid root ceremony over the derived address, and the address itself is Keccak256("WARDEN/seed/v1" || root_pubkey33 || salt32) computed on-chain, so the PDA cannot be squatted with an attacker-controlled root: a different root derives a different address, and the victim's address cannot be reached without the victim's passkey.
notes: CLOSED by Phase 1B Task 2b. Also referred to as WRD-PoP-01 in the Phase 1B plan prose; WRD-ROOT-01 is the canonical id. RED evidence: at d0072fd an executable exploit created the victim's PDA under the attacker's root and locked the victim out (task-2b-report.md). The seed derivation is stronger than Squads' fix (require create_key to sign) because it needs no extra signer. Two Phase-1A gaps close with it: creation is now top-level-only, and an off-curve root x cannot be created because the precompile cannot verify a signature under a point it cannot decompress. Cost: MAX_MINTS_AT_CREATE fell from 4 to 1 (see WRD-BUF-05). Keep the squat-race negative test forever. Evidence sha 50dc590 is the Task 2b commit itself.

title: Root instructions are transaction-level only
statement: Every root instruction requires get_stack_height() == TRANSACTION_LEVEL_STACK_HEIGHT, so a root path can never be invoked through a middleman program.
notes: Landed in 26a8c1e. The negative test drives a real CPI caller (programs/test-middleman, test-only, never deployed) rather than stubbing the stack height, which is the only version of this test worth having. Distinct from the pre-existing self-CPI rejection, which only blocks warden->warden. Adopted from LazorKit (MIT). Held at test-covered, not higher: one caller shape is proven, not the whole space of intermediate programs.

title: User verification is mandatory
statement: authenticatorData must have both UP and UV set; a UP-only assertion is rejected.
notes: The credential is created with userVerification: required and ES256 only; the on-chain UV check is what makes that client-side request non-advisory.

title: rpIdHash is SHA-256 of the FULL origin, read from state
statement: rp_id_hash equals SHA-256("chrome-extension://<id>") -- not SHA-256("<id>") -- it is recomputed on-chain from the stored origin at creation, read from SmartAccount state on every verification, and never taken from caller-supplied instruction data or a compiled-in literal.
notes: The naive reading of the WebAuthn spec rejects EVERY assertion; measured in spike 2b. Open L9 lane, NOT covered by this invariant: the extension id changes between a dev-loaded and a store build and there is no migration path for an account created under the old one.

title: Precompile binding and ordering
statement: The root path binds exactly one secp256r1 precompile instruction, named by index in its own instruction data, at a lower index than the warden instruction, executed by the real secp256r1 program id, carrying exactly one signature whose (pubkey, message, signature) equal (root.pubkey, authenticatorData || SHA256(clientDataJSON), sig).
notes: L0 DEPENDENCY NOW SATISFIED (26a8c1e): programs/warden/tests/sigverify_wiring.rs asserts BOTH directions -- a valid signature makes the transaction succeed, and a forged one is rejected by the precompile, not by us. Only the pair proves the runtime actually runs ECDSA; either alone is compatible with a harness that verifies nothing. litesvm must stay pinned with the `precompiles` feature (LiteSVM::default() starts with every feature off) and .claude/test-gate.sh additionally asserts the feature RESOLVES -- which is a different failure mode from the runtime gate, so both are required. `fee_payer_identity_neither_authorizes_nor_blocks` is the control that stops the whole suite passing on the outer transaction signature.

title: Strict depth-0 clientDataJSON scanner
statement: clientDataJSON is rejected above MAX_CLIENT_DATA_LEN (512 B); the object is walked at depth 0 only; exactly one top-level type/challenge/origin is required and any duplicate top-level key rejects; JSON escapes are decoded before comparison or the value is rejected; type == "webauthn.get"; origin equals the stored origin; challenge equals base64url(transcript hash); a present crossOrigin must be the JSON boolean false. Byte-substring matching is forbidden.
notes: LazorKit's regression vector {"tokenBinding":{"id":"x}y"},"challenge":"real"} -- a } inside a nested string desynced their brace-depth tracker and mis-located challenge -- is ported and rejected. This is one of the two designated Trident fuzz targets (L4); the other is the 1B ExecutePayload parser.

title: cluster_tag domain separation
statement: cluster_tag is a 32-byte client-attested domain separator stored at creation, non-zero-checked, immutable in 1A, and bound into the transcript so an assertion produced against one stored tag cannot be replayed against an account holding a different tag.
notes: STATED LIMIT: it is NOT a verified genesis binding. A Solana program cannot read the cluster's genesis hash, so the value is whatever the extension wrote at create_account. It does not guarantee the tag names the cluster the transaction lands on. Codex flagged this in the 1A pilot as a finding; it was adjudicated a false positive because transcript.rs:69-76 documents the deferral -- in a file the reviewer had not been shown. That is why sibling files are now mandatory in every review prompt.

title: Generation-bump semantics (helper-driven)
statement: A transcript carrying a generation other than the account's current generation is rejected, and a session's authority is scoped to the generation it was granted under.
notes: EVIDENCE CAVEAT, STATED PLAINLY: the covering tests advance `generation` through a test helper / a revoke-and-regrant cycle, NOT through a real `execute_recovery`. They prove the CHECK, not the BUMP. The property that actually matters to a user -- that recovery invalidates every outstanding assertion, session, stage and pending action -- is WRD-ROOT-11, seeded at `unimplemented` because `execute_recovery` is Phase 1C and does not exist.

title: action_hash binds the complete semantic inputs
statement: action_hash = Keccak256(op_type:u8 || borsh(op_args)) where op_args contains every semantic input of the instruction the root authorises; the program recomputes it from the instruction it is executing and rejects on mismatch, so no argument or account can be swapped after the passkey ceremony.
notes: The op_type byte is the discriminator LZR-ACC-M2 was missing; op_bytes_are_distinct + op_bytes_are_pinned keep it from collapsing. 1B extends op_args to execute/swap (the exact compiled instruction list, or the Stage hash) and that re-opens this invariant for those ops. 2026-08-21 (Task 6 swap round 1): root swap now binds the EXACT route bytes via SwapBody.route_hash = Keccak256(route_data) (WRDF-0058), so a captured assertion cannot substitute the route_plan/quote/staged content.

title: Transcript preimage byte layout is pinned across the language boundary
statement: transcript_hash = Keccak256("WARDEN/root/v1" || cluster_tag[32] || program_id[32] || account[32] || generation:u64LE || policy_version:u32LE || root_nonce:u64LE || expiry_ts:i64LE || signed_slot:u64LE || action_hash[32]), and the Rust program, the packages/core TS mirror and the IDL agree on it byte for byte.

evidence.name: does not treat expiryTs and signedSlot as interchangeable

notes: HELD DOWN DELIBERATELY -- the layout is right, the GATE is missing. 26a8c1e added signed_slot to Rust, the packages/core mirror and the IDL together, and both sides pin vectors including a max-slot one and an adjacency test (expiry_ts and signed_slot are adjacent fixed-width integers, so a mirror that swapped them would still hash something). But the vectors are HAND-SYNCED: the TS test hard-codes hex copied from the Rust test, so a coordinated edit to both drifts silently and nothing fails. Only a generated cross-language golden-vector gate (Task 9 / L9) promotes this row. LZR-ACC-H2 is exactly this class.

title: Recovery invalidates everything outstanding
statement: A successful execute_recovery replaces the root and increments generation, and that increment invalidates every outstanding assertion, session, stage and pending action -- proven end to end through the real instruction, not a test helper.
notes: Seeded now because WRD-ROOT-08's evidence advances `generation` via a helper and a revoke/regrant cycle, which proves the CHECK but not the BUMP. Without this row the ledger would read as if recovery invalidation were already covered. Phase 1C.

title: Fixed deny-list, on both paths, above the registry
statement: SetAuthority, Approve, ApproveChecked and Revoke on SPL Token and Token-2022 are rejected in the execute payload decoder on BOTH the session and the root path, before dispatch and before any registry lookup; CloseAccount is rejected unless ALL of: it is a direct payload instruction (not nested inside another program's CPI), the account's amount_before is exactly 0, the decoded destination is the SmartAccount PDA, and the account is neither the PDA itself nor a Mint.
notes: Instruction tags (SetAuthority 6, Approve 4, Revoke 5, CloseAccount 9, ApproveChecked 13) are UNVERIFIED against SPL source. The implementer re-derives each from spl-token's TokenInstruction enum at the pinned crate version, records crate version + source path in docs/program/PHASE1B-MEASUREMENTS.md, and a unit test asserts each constant equals what the crate encodes. A wrong tag here is a silent hole, not a compile error. The decoder is a whitelist of closes it can PROVE, not a blacklist of closes it dislikes. 2026-08-21 (Task 8, WRDF-0073): parse_payload accepts a writable idx-0 structurally (the writable-PDA rule lives in enforce_pda_writable), and the TS codec now matches — so the deny-list's one CloseAccount exception (rent to the PDA) is expressible through the canonical SDK. Cross-language fixture programs/warden/tests/fixtures/payload_writable_pda_close.bin pins the parity. B4 (2026-08-23): the deny-scan unit test now parametrises over BOTH SPL Token and Token-2022 for all four tags (8 cases); previously only SPL Token was exercised, so the 'and Token-2022' half of the statement was unproven. Root-path SetAuthority added.

title: No registry entry can re-enable a denied pair
statement: A registry (or policy) list containing a denied (program, instruction) pair still fails closed: the decoder runs first, there is no override flag, and the deny-list is unreachable by the section 5.4 loosening lattice.
notes: Section 5.4 says loosening EXTENDS the registry, so a deny that lived only in the registry would not be a floor at all -- and the root path skips the registry entirely, so a deny enforced at registry_allows would not cover the root path in any form. The required negative test is a registry list containing SetAuthority that still fails closed. B4 (2026-08-23): previously ZERO coverage. The new test plants a real registry entry for (SPL_TOKEN_ID, SetAuthority) in list 1 and asserts DENY_LISTED — not RegistryDenied — which is what proves the decoder runs BEFORE the registry rather than the registry merely failing to match. A companion control test proves the planting back door is not inert (a benign planted selector IS honoured), so the main assertion cannot pass vacuously.

title: A squatted Stage is recoverable
statement: A stranger who pre-computes a victim's staged content cannot block or squat the victim's Stage: the PDA binds the creator (['stage', account, creator, hash]), so the stranger's stage and the victim's are different addresses and the victim's stage_open always succeeds — the ND-SQD3-LO-01 creator-less-seed squat is closed by construction, not merely time-boxed.
notes: Task 4. Two firms with two methods hit this exact class on Squads: Neodyme ND-SQD3-LO-01 (TransactionBuffer seeded [multisig, buffer_index], 256 slots, one Initiate-permission member fills all 256 with unclosable garbage) and Certora H-01 (transaction buffer may become inaccessible and unclosable). Seeds must bind the creator, or the count must be unbounded-but-cleanable -- pick one and test the other's failure mode.

title: No unbounded uncleanable buffer
statement: There is no per-account fixed slot table an attacker can exhaust (each (account, creator, content) is its own PDA), and every Stage — finalized or not — has a permissionless closure path after expiry_ts that returns the rent to its creator (Certora H-01 lifecycle GC).
notes: Task 4. The vault must never fund Stage rent (spec 5.2 rule 4: account creation is always funded by the outer fee payer), or the squat becomes a rent drain of the shape audited on revoke_session.

title: Every root-ceremony transaction fits the 1232-byte packet
statement: A complete root ceremony transaction (secp256r1 precompile instruction + the warden instruction) serialises to at most MAX_TX_BYTES = 1232 for freeze, unfreeze, a 2-cap grant_session, and root transfer of SOL and of an SPL token.
notes: The budget is tight: the 1A root ceremony uses 680 B, leaving ~552 B of payload headroom, and clientDataJSON may legally grow to 512 B. WRD-NONCE-03's signed_slot consumes part of that headroom -- 1B RE-MEASURES and these tests must be re-run, not assumed.

title: Every session transaction fits the 1232-byte packet
statement: A session-signed transfer of SOL and of an SPL token each serialise to at most MAX_TX_BYTES = 1232.
notes: The 40-account cap on session execute is PROVISIONAL and byte-driven, not CU-driven: a real 43-account Jupiter route serialised to 1,235 B while a 35-account route fit. That 35-43 band is a totalKeys measurement; writableKeys and executeAccountCount were never captured. 1B must re-derive it.

title: create_account packet limits are measured, not assumed
statement: A create_account transaction carrying its mandatory proof-of-possession ceremony fits the 1232-byte packet at MAX_MINTS_AT_CREATE = 1 mint (cap + ceiling + threshold) and does NOT fit at 2, and more than MAX_MINTS_AT_CREATE mints is rejected on-chain.
notes: Re-measured for Phase 1B Task 2b: proof of possession adds 477 B (182 B precompile instruction, 226 B RootArgs, the Instructions sysvar account), so 0 mints = 949 B, 1 mint = 1117 B, 2 mints = 1285 B (53 B over) and MAX_MINTS_AT_CREATE dropped 4 -> 1. Mints 2..8 are added later by Phase 1C set_policy. The negative tests are the load-bearing half: they are what stops a future constant bump from producing unlandable transactions. create_with_pop_transaction_sizes_are_measured_and_bounded asserts the constant EQUALS the largest count that actually fits, so it cannot drift from the measurement. Evidence sha 50dc590 is the Task 2b commit itself.

title: stage_finalize checks the content hash and records generation + policy_version
statement: stage_finalize requires written == len and Keccak256(data) == hash (the content-address is verified, not assumed), and records the bound SmartAccount's live generation and policy_version — the account PDA re-derived from its stored seed so a planted copy cannot supply a forged generation. The execute-time consume/current-state check is WRD-STAGE-02.
notes: Task 4. TOB-SQUADS-8 is the adjacent class: ephemeral signer seeds derived only from the batch key rather than per transaction, so all transactions in a batch shared one ephemeral keypair. Any PDA whose seeds do not uniquely bind (tx index, creator, nonce) reproduces it -- which is why Stage addressing and execute's invoke_signed seeds are both in scope here.

title: Staged content is single-use and bound to current account state at execution
statement: execute (root or session) accepts a finalized Stage only when its recorded generation and policy_version still equal the account's current values, verifies Keccak256(stage.data) == the signed payload_hash, and closes the Stage on success so it cannot be replayed; a failed execute reverts, leaving the Stage and the root nonce intact for retry.
notes: Task 5 (execute). The finalize half is WRD-STAGE-01 (test-covered at Task 4); this consume half needs execute, which does not exist yet. B4 (2026-08-23): the generation and policy_version currency bindings — the substance of 'bound to CURRENT account state' — now have execute-side tests (stale-policy_version and stale-generation both rejected with StageInvalid, session path deliberately, since policy_version is inside the root transcript and a root variant would fail earlier with ChallengeMismatch). Root-nonce-intact-on-failure is asserted on the empty-staged-payload test.

title: Unit layer: per-mint net outflow, coalesced and floored
statement: compare_and_account returns outflow per mint computed from before/after snapshots: multiple vault ATAs of one mint coalesce into a single entry, intra-vault rebalances net to zero, and inflow floors to zero rather than crediting a negative outflow.
notes: UNIT LAYER ONLY (campaign plan G7): synthetic snapshots, no CPI in the loop. End-to-end enforcement through execute is WRD-EXEC-*, unimplemented until Task 5. Added retrospectively by A0; the module landed in Task 1 (f0f38ca, fixes 2023902/d394b74).

title: Unit layer: one SOL equation across WSOL and PDA lamports
statement: Wrapped-SOL value is measured by LAMPORTS, not the cached `amount`, and is decided by `is_native` (which must agree with the native mint key or the account is rejected); wrapped-SOL and PDA lamport deltas merge into one SOL number, floored once, and a native mint key never appears in by_mint.
notes: UNIT LAYER ONLY. Non-WSOL CloseAccount rent folds into the same SOL sum (a_close_to_a_stranger_charges_the_rent_as_sol_outflow). See WRD-CONS-01 note for scope. WRDF-0008 (A0 round 3): classification was mint-key-only and would have split a Token-2022 native account's delta into by_mint[9pan…]; fixed to is_native-first with both native mint keys as belt-and-braces (compare.rs account_amount, constants::NATIVE_MINT_2022 verified against vendored spl-token-2022 7.0.0 src/native_mint.rs). RED verified: the new test fails against the pre-fix classification. WRDF-0011 (A0 round 6): native value was measured by `amount`, a SyncNative-updated cache — a SyncNative+Transfer pair drained an unsynced donation with amount unchanged. Now measured by lamports, and is_native must agree with the native mint key (mismatch rejected). RED verified.

title: Unit layer: authority or identity mutation is a reject, never an accounting entry
statement: Any change to a vault token account's owner, delegate, close authority, state, is_native, data length, TLV tail, runtime program owner, or backing-mint identity/authorities is InstructionRejected/ConservationViolated — it is never converted into an outflow number; pre-existing delegates and close authorities reject even when unchanged.
notes: UNIT LAYER ONLY. owner_program in Snap is what closes the SWIG-ACC-C1 fake-layout class at this layer; the through-CPI test is Task 5's swig_acc_c1_close_and_reopen_under_fake_layout_rejected. WRDF-0012 (A0 round 6): several unmodeled T22 mint extensions (MintCloseAuthority, InterestBearingConfig, MetadataPointer, group/member pointers, ScaledUiAmountConfig, PausableConfig) carry reassignable authorities no compared field would see, and the mint tail hash is never compared; 1B now fails closed on any required mint with an unmodeled extension. RED verified.

title: Unit layer: accounts cannot appear, vanish, or move without an explanation
statement: A vault token account that disappears without a matching CloseIntent, appears vault-owned only in the AFTER snapshot, changes list position, or duplicates another pubkey is rejected; a legal vault-sweep close is counted once and only once.
notes: UNIT LAYER ONLY. The became-vault-owned rejection (NewVaultAccountRejected, 6051) is round-1 fix C2, evidenced here directly. See WRD-CONS-01 note for scope. Prior art corrected per WRDF-0005: LZR-ACC-C1 is the position-vs-identity class; TOB-SQUADS-7 (unauthenticated creation) belongs to WRD-ROOT-01, not here.

title: Unit layer: strict, fail-closed SPL / Token-2022 layout parsing
statement: Classic SPL parses only exactly 82-byte mints and 165-byte token accounts; COption tags other than 0/1 are parse errors; T22 TLV tails are walked bounded and fail closed, danger extensions each set their bit, and transfer-fee authorities are extracted by TLV type rather than hashed with the whole tail.
notes: UNIT LAYER ONLY. spl_crate_layout_lengths_are_pinned ties the 82/165 constants to the pinned spl-token crate so a dependency bump cannot silently move the layout. See WRD-CONS-01 note for scope.

title: Unit layer: conservation arithmetic cannot wrap
statement: Outflow summation uses checked arithmetic and rejects on overflow instead of wrapping; a crafted pair of snapshots whose deltas sum past u64::MAX is an error, not a small outflow.
notes: UNIT LAYER ONLY. clippy::arithmetic_side_effects is denied crate-wide as the static half of this claim. See WRD-CONS-01 note for scope.

title: Root key non-exportable, never in extension memory
statement: Warden exposes no root-export API and root private-key material never enters extension memory; session and recovery secrets are typed and cannot be used as root authority. (A platform-synced passkey may itself be backup-eligible and movable by the OS/authenticator — that is the T7 threat, outside Warden's enforcement; Warden's boundary is that IT never exports or holds root material.)
notes: Seeded by C0 (campaign plan 2026-08-20); implemented by client C2. WRDF-0024 narrowed the claim from 'non-exportable': a backup-eligible synced passkey is movable by the platform; Warden's enforceable boundary is no Warden export API and no root material in extension memory. Commit 36c7e4bee57dba4b2b7efce498d25818bcba4fb3 creates apps/extension but only owns a typed derived unwrap key; it has no WebAuthn ceremony, root-key representation, root/session conversion, provider, or export surface. Safe absence is not a completed production invariant, and the synced-passkey T7 owner decision remains open, so status stays `unimplemented`.

title: No retained password; no equality-check auth
statement: No plaintext password is retained after derivation; no password equality check substitutes for fresh cryptographic authentication.
notes: Seeded by C0; implemented by C2/C5. Status remains PARTIAL. The core has no password equality surface: every attempt derives a KEK and succeeds only through authenticated DEK unwrap. Record orchestration overwrites caller-owned password/PRF/plaintext buffers, but cannot erase a password that ever existed as a JS string. Commit 36c7e4bee57dba4b2b7efce498d25818bcba4fb3 stores only an already-derived KEK in trusted storage.session. Commit bddb0ccbab2aa55780b132fd1528b03a297e2124 adds the first extension password consumer: it snapshots and synchronously overwrites caller bytes, derives from the exact canonical record metadata, authenticates that record and full context, schema-validates and clears plaintext before activation, and never caches the password. Commit 8653fed0b922e37a3998e96ca3f33f686daeeba7 makes record v2 own the complete context, removes normal caller context selection, and requires retained-KEK wake restore to authenticate and schema-check the exact record before readiness. Commit 125ad761b3af1879f42fa13135e5a07d57721223 moves production record seal/open to revocable asynchronous Argon2id, wipes owned password copies on every path, and proves in real Chrome that a host task preempts the RFC-profile derivation and abort rejects without activating. Wrong-password, wake-tamper, and pending-derivation tests prove no session remains active. The compound row stays `unimplemented`: no browser-reachable prompt/re-prompt exists, no production Argon2 floor or attempt-rate/backoff policy is selected, below-floor records remain accepted, PRF device behavior is unverified, the measured Chrome 151 server is not the slowest supported device, and JS/VM zeroization is best effort.

title: Absolute wall-clock unlock deadlines
statement: Idle and hard unlock deadlines are absolute wall-clock values, checked on every key use and after every service-worker wake; expiry clears all session unlock material.
notes: Seeded by C0; implemented by C2. MV3 suspension is the threat; status remains PARTIAL. Core and extension lanes cover absolute idle/hard instants, live-clock checks, one stable AbortSignal, trusted-only v2 storage, synchronous lock/expiry/record-change abort and best-effort buffer clearing, late-result suppression, and selective serialized cleanup. Commits 36c7e4bee57dba4b2b7efce498d25818bcba4fb3, c3b74eb3e93c9dde6eb29141d737e49bbc57c16f, and 0e3fc0f7b7119f41777c8dbbb98eecdef26db34a establish those layers. Commit bddb0ccbab2aa55780b132fd1528b03a297e2124 adds authenticated record-to-session activation and a real seed-use lease with nested deadline/revocation/readback checks; tests prove pending replacement, unnotified swap, disappearance, and late-output cleanup. Commit 8653fed0b922e37a3998e96ca3f33f686daeeba7 upgrades wake restore from a public bundle-id check to retained-KEK authentication, strict signer-payload decode, account/bundle comparison, live-deadline checks, and exact record readback before readiness resolves true; tamper failure revokes and removes the session. Commit 125ad761b3af1879f42fa13135e5a07d57721223 adds one pending-derivation AbortController owned by the extension lifecycle. Lock, replace, clear, competing unlock, and restore revoke it; a late derivation cannot activate. A deterministic race test proves restore clears and refuses a session serialized by a just-superseded same-owner unlock. Real Chrome proves background-priority Argon2 abort rejection, while hosts without `scheduler.postTask` may still finish an initialized KDF before output suppression and WebCrypto remains non-cancellable. The row remains `unimplemented`: no browser-reachable signer, real-key wake/signature vector, approval/hardware owners, authenticated external freshness, or durable cleanup guarantee exists. Chrome cleanup rejection can leave KEK bytes, and a callback must not perform an irreversible side effect before the final check. Audit finding A-2 (Low) recorded the half of "checked ... after every service-worker wake" that the lazy check alone cannot carry: nothing woke the worker AT the deadline, so the serialized unwrap key stayed in `chrome.storage.session` past both deadlines until the worker next woke for an unrelated reason. Commit 215663fd8b69389e87dee8c1ac8a870834412c64 makes expiry EAGER as well as lazy — the manifest declares `alarms`, `UnlockSessionOwner` keeps one one-shot `warden.unlock-session.expiry` alarm armed at min(idle, hard) across activation/touch/restore and clears it on lock, and the background registers the `onAlarm` listener synchronously at worker startup. The alarm supplies only the OCCASION: it invokes exactly the same `isUnlocked`/`assertActive` path every key use runs, so the abort/zeroise/remove behaviour keeps one implementation. The lazy check therefore remains the authority and this row's status is unchanged, deliberately: Chrome may delay a sub-30-second alarm and may drop alarms across a browser restart, the alarms port is optional (absent = exactly the pre-A-2 behaviour) and a failing port can never fail an otherwise valid unlock, and none of this is browser-measured — no real `chrome.alarms` delivery, MV3 eviction, or clock-change experiment was run. The window is narrowed, not closed.

title: Versioned AEAD keyring envelope with contextual AAD
statement: Encrypted keyring envelopes are versioned AEAD with random nonces and AAD binding account, full extension origin, key kind, schema version, canonical cluster identity (genesis hash), and Warden program id; malformed, unknown-version, replayed-context (incl. cross-cluster), and tampered envelopes reject.
notes: Seeded by C0; implemented by C2. AAD must not bind a release hash; genesis plus program id are required because a SmartAccount PDA is not network-qualified. Status remains PARTIAL. Core tests cover strict contextual AES-256-GCM envelopes, independent password/PRF KEK wraps of one random DEK, authenticated outer metadata, canonical bounded records, hostile version/length/cost inputs, tamper/splice/cross-context rejection, deadline races, and cleanup. Commits 7e18f275a839c2d88427a104b5814bb266fe445d, c3b74eb3e93c9dde6eb29141d737e49bbc57c16f, and 0e3fc0f7b7119f41777c8dbbb98eecdef26db34a add trusted local ownership, v2 bundle binding, and live change revocation. Commit bddb0ccbab2aa55780b132fd1528b03a297e2124 defines the AAD-bound session-signer v1 plaintext as exactly a 32-byte Ed25519 seed, composes record mutation with revocation, authenticates the exact record and supplied full context on activation/use, and suppresses output when exact readback changes. Commit 8653fed0b922e37a3998e96ca3f33f686daeeba7 makes binary record v2 self-contain canonical copy-owned AAD context, forbids caller context on v2, derives extension origin from browser runtime id, strictly tests context parser boundaries/tamper, authenticates wake restore, and leaves v1 available only for explicit core migration while the extension refuses it. Commit 125ad761b3af1879f42fa13135e5a07d57721223 exact-pins `@noble/hashes` 2.4.0, attests it in the deploy verifier, and moves production record seal/open to the asynchronous path; a real self-only-CSP Chrome extension measures RFC-profile output, host-task progress, cancellation, and password wiping. Commit cafced9c2f4725e0a95afc792fd0290acc01d28b exposes callback-lifetime copies of the already-authenticated account, genesis hash, and Warden program id and makes the still-unreachable coordinator refuse any mismatch before final key use. The row stays `unimplemented`: there is still no record-creation/onboarding or migration flow, selected production Argon2 floor, rejection/upgrade policy for below-floor records, PRF device matrix, real authoritative context resolver, browser-reachable privileged consumer, on-chain grant match, external freshness, or CAS/durability guarantee. Valid same-context replay and cleanup-retained KEK bytes remain possible. Audit finding K-1 (Medium) recorded the half of this statement that the AEAD alone cannot carry: authenticated AAD proves a context was not EDITED, never that it is a context the adopting client is allowed to accept, because a whole record can be REPLACED by a differently sealed one. The extension-side comparison is now its own row, WRD-EXT-03 (`test-covered` at 27039aaa3e5f3130d32e2c55364b1af6b1962705); this row's own status is unchanged. WRDF-0122 was CONFIRMED by a RED regression at 92cec87dcca1c49a9f87e3afef11d06f3db319d8: `pnpm --filter @warden/core exec vitest run test/keyring-record.test.ts -t "WRDF-0122"` exited 1 because a password open recovered the caller-mutated plaintext instead of the entry snapshot. Commit d786b9993370d048c0183e258c8b5cfb4a677e35 snapshots PRF output and plaintext, clears the caller buffers, and uses/wipes only private copies before asynchronous password derivation. At that exact SHA, the focused command passed 1/1 and `pnpm --filter @warden/core exec vitest run test/keyring-record.test.ts test/keyring-record-v2.test.ts test/keyring-bundle.test.ts test/keyring-derive-async.test.ts` passed 52/52. Full repository-gate verification remains pending. WRDF-0123 was CONFIRMED by a RED regression at 3c11151ed0c67aa5a173888bd6deaafe5df96120: `pnpm --filter @warden/core exec vitest run test/keyring-record.test.ts -t "WRDF-0123"` exited 1 because a Buffer plaintext reopened as zeroes rather than its entry value; the same fixture covers overlapping ordinary Uint8Array password/plaintext views. Commit f34ba60bbe639a8266d1853d70b35b81782fb172 copies all three secret inputs into disjoint base-class Uint8Arrays before clearing any caller view. At that exact SHA, the focused command passed 1/1 and `pnpm --filter @warden/core exec vitest run test/keyring-record.test.ts test/keyring-record-v2.test.ts test/keyring-bundle.test.ts test/keyring-derive-async.test.ts` passed 53/53. Full repository-gate verification remains pending.

title: Browser-owned message provenance
statement: Privileged background methods derive origin, extension id, tab, and frame from browser-owned sender metadata, never page-supplied data.
notes: Seeded by C0; implemented by client C1 (the MV3 trust boundary). Commit fcf4a255e0809a41f6b8033db12b0fb4762ff40e adds the browser-owned provider/UI sender classifiers. Commit 16663cb347707fc564698a9ac76a29ee987e9bd0 adds the strict closed provider-request parser. Commit 2975296eeff4f1096146174be41649ec399590b5 imports both provider controls into the emitted worker behind a named runtime Port: one frozen provenance tuple owns copied requests, independent 128-bit Web Crypto ids, duplicate-correlation rejection, exact-object settlement, bounded per-Port/global state, absolute expiry, and disconnect/malformed/disposal cancellation. Commit 26f3904c1d1497d81c8d3727387e62f0cc651f2a corrects the first runtime composition: Chrome requires MV3 wake listeners synchronously at top-level, so the zero-authority listener exists before storage promises settle. Commit 692e5509f7b4a62a8082aaccff2b9b89b8af315e adds the default-isolated HTTP(S) bridge; real Chromium measures frame provenance, navigation, and worker stop/wake. Commit 14205821687cf3da51abfa12866985e2a545b15a adds the exact-name router and closed action-popup route. Commit 65df16854c1ecfbb5e288091c6dc4d76bd10b700 adds a separate approval-page classifier that derives the request id only from Chrome's exact sender URL and requires this extension id/origin, documentId, tab id, frame 0, and active-at-connect lifecycle. The route accepts a matching payload id only as confirmation; a real isolated content-script world that shares sender.id is disconnected from both popup and approval channels. Status stays `unimplemented`: provider creation/success remains absent, the approval lane can only read/reject/cancel, and no signed consequence yet proves browser provenance on a successful privileged path. Same-page scripts can still forge or suppress page-bridge traffic.

title: Privileged UI port requires proven extension identity
statement: An extension UI port is privileged only when sender.id == chrome.runtime.id AND browser-owned sender.url/origin is the exact chrome-extension://<id> origin at an allowed extension-page path; extension-id equality alone is insufficient because an extension-owned content script shares sender.id and can call runtime.connect.
notes: Seeded by C0; implemented by C1. WRDF-0021: id equality alone lets a content script impersonate privileged UI. Commit fcf4a255e0809a41f6b8033db12b0fb4762ff40e adds the exact extension-origin/path classifier. Commit 14205821687cf3da51abfa12866985e2a545b15a wires the closed action-popup lane and browser-measures the real tabless action sender plus a rejected isolated-content-script forgery. Commit 65df16854c1ecfbb5e288091c6dc4d76bd10b700 adds the distinct full-page `/approval.html?request=req_<128-bit hex>` lane. It requires exact browser-owned extension id, origin, URL serialization, documentId, tab id, frame 0, and Port lifetime; duplicate request/document Ports and more than 16 pages reject. Its closed schema has only getReview/reject, its owner surface has only read/reject/cancel, and content-script forgery disconnects in real Chromium. The page bundle is structurally limited to UI plus protocol modules. Status stays `unimplemented`: no approve/sign method consumes this identity, Chrome 106/store/manual compatibility remains unverified, and the action popup still lacks browser-supplied per-document identity.

title: Keyring record adoption is pinned to the whole expected context
statement: The background adopts an encrypted keyring record only when every context field this build pins equals its own expectation — full extension origin, cluster genesis hash, and Warden program id (key kind and plaintext schema version are pinned by the record parser) — so a validly sealed record naming another cluster or another Warden deployment is refused on password unlock, on record replacement, and on wake restore, before any unlock session is created or kept.

evidence.name: refuses a password unlock of a validly sealed record from a foreign cluster
refuses a password unlock of a validly sealed record from a foreign Warden deployment
refuses to store a foreign-cluster replacement record and keeps the live session
refuses to store a foreign-deployment replacement record and keeps the live session
refuses to restore a wake session whose record names a foreign cluster
rejects a record sealed for another extension origin before activating a session
equals the core public genesis pin for the chain it names

notes: Seeded and landed together by audit finding K-1 (Medium) in commit 27039aaa3e5f3130d32e2c55364b1af6b1962705. K-1: a record v2 context is AAD-authenticated, so it cannot be EDITED without the KEK, but a whole record can be REPLACED by a different, validly sealed one. `contextForRecord` compared only `origin` and took genesisHash/programId/account from the very record it was deciding whether to trust, so the WRD-KEY-04 cross-cluster rejection held at the AEAD layer and not at this trust boundary. A Warden SmartAccount PDA is not network-qualified, so the same address exists on devnet and mainnet. The expectation is now a required constructor input (`KeyringLifecycleOptions.expectedContext`), injected exactly like `expectedOrigin` and never chosen inside the class; a build with no pin is not constructible. `account` is deliberately NOT compared: it is the record's own legitimate choice and the extension has no build-level expectation for it. LIMITS, stated rather than implied. (1) The shipped pin is `solana:mainnet` byte literals in `apps/extension/src/background/expected-keyring-context.ts`, created because the extension had no cluster pin of its own and the core module publishing the public genesis/program pins is forbidden in the background bundle by `scripts/build.mjs`. That chain choice is an UNCONFIRMED release decision awaiting the owner; changing it stops every record sealed under the previous pin from unlocking, by design. `test/expected-keyring-context.test.ts` is a drift guard against the core constants, not evidence that the chain is the right one. (2) Nothing in the shipped extension creates a keyring record yet, so this refusal is exercised only against test-sealed records. (3) WRD-KEY-04 and WRD-EXT-01/02 stay `unimplemented` for their own separate reasons; this row certifies only the adoption comparison.

title: Approval control arms only after a focused dwell and trusted input
statement: The approval window's approve control is armed only after the window has held focus continuously for the reviewed dwell, a trusted pointer move has occurred inside the document since the review response landed, and no focus or visibility loss has intervened; an approve request is sent only for a trusted activation whose pointerdown/pointerup pair — or Enter/Space keydown — happened after that arm time, and every other input is refused silently, leaving the request pending. The approval window is opened at a per-launch randomised position that keeps it fully on screen.

evidence.name: arms only once an uninterrupted focus dwell and one trusted pointer move are both complete
restarts the whole dwell on focus loss and requires a fresh pointer move
refuses an untrusted click even with a fully armed control
refuses a click whose pointerdown was primed before the arm time
accepts a trusted Enter or Space activation only after the arm time
refuses an already-evidenced click when focus is lost before it arrives
derives left and top from the injected RNG across the whole placement range
clamps a hostile or broken RNG onto the screen instead of failing the launch

notes: Seeded and landed together by audit finding A-1 (Low now, Medium the day signing ships) in commit 699beec72a84889a67c0d134249ba01966da5ac5. A-1: the approve control was armed synchronously with the review response and the click handler accepted any `click` event — no dwell, no focus settle, no `event.isTrusted`, no requirement that the press/release pair followed arming — while the window opened at a fixed, page-predictable position. A page that primes rapid clicks or keypresses at those coordinates could land the user's next input on "Approve and sign". The decision now lives in one pure module with no DOM handle, no timer and no clock of its own, so every rule is proven over passed-in timestamps rather than DOM timing; `main.ts` feeds it browser events and never re-implements a rule. APPROVAL_ARM_DWELL_MS is 600 ms, the midpoint of the audit's 500-700 ms band. A focus or visibility loss clears the dwell AND the pointer move AND any primed press, which is what makes "the last loss did not occur within the dwell" hold by construction. Placement is drawn per launch from an injected RNG (default `Math.random`) over the inclusive range that keeps the 720x600 window inside an assumed 1024x768 display. LIMITS, stated rather than implied. (1) The shipped bundle still cannot approve anything: `canApprove` is false in production and `scripts/build.mjs` keeps the provider pipeline off the worker, so this guard is armed ahead of the capability it protects, which is exactly what the audit asked for and also means no shipped path exercises it. (2) It governs only when the PAGE is willing to send an approve request; the background still owns the record, the digest, and the single atomic winner (WRD-APR-01..03). (3) Placement randomness is a jitter, not a secret — it raises the cost of pre-computing the button position, it does not make it unknowable — and an MV3 worker has no screen metrics, so the bounds are an assumed minimum display rather than the real one; adding `system.display` was judged not worth the permission. (4) Nothing here is browser-measured: there is no real Chromium input-stream evidence, no real overlay or cross-origin framing experiment, and pointer timestamps are compared at-or-after the arm time rather than strictly after, because a trusted pointermove and the pointerdown that follows it can share a millisecond. (5) WRD-EXT-01/02 stay `unimplemented` for their own reasons; this row certifies only the arming decision and the placement draw. (6) ACCESSIBILITY CONSEQUENCE, needing an owner decision: the human-presence condition is a trusted POINTER move, so a keyboard-only user who never moves a pointer can never arm the control. That is deliberate and is the stronger reading — a primed keypress stream is part of the same threat, and accepting a trusted keydown as presence would let such a stream arm the control after the dwell — but it means the approve path is not reachable by keyboard alone. Revisit before signing is enabled in a shipped build.

title: Page promises settle only over the transferred capability port
statement: A main-world provider request promise resolves with signed transaction bytes, or rejects with a terminal failure, only on a message delivered over the single MessagePort the isolated content owner transferred into the document in answer to the one capability claim that owner posted as it was constructed; the content owner answers only the first claim in a document and never mints a second channel, the page owner claims only the first grant it observes and refuses and counts every later one, the port reference is private to the owning instance and is never echoed, logged, or re-posted, and a same-window same-origin message carrying the correct correlationId, the correct expiresAt, and a well-formed receiptId is ignored against a pending request.

evidence.name: ignores a well-formed same-window terminal forgery against a pending request
never settles a request while no capability has been granted
claims the first capability grant and refuses every later one
refuses malformed and wrong-context capability grants without claiming one
closes every pending promise when the granted port cannot be bound
disposal rejects every pending promise, closes the capability, and is idempotent
posts exactly one capability claim as it is constructed
answers only the first capability claim in a document
refuses to settle a page promise from a same-window forgery end to end
carries one C16 promise over one lost Port without minting a second page request
real Chromium returns exactly the reviewed message after one authenticated signature
C20 resend reaches one C14/C19 terminal result after real MV3 worker death

notes: Seeded and landed together by audit finding X-1 (Low, gated) in commit 69a6282c7dea5e959e17e02dcc49c86ca5450898, with the handshake direction corrected in 243f469d1f40d34922785acea2cd598614f10845. X-1: the page owner authenticated a terminal response by event.source === window, event.origin === documentOrigin, and a correlationId/expiresAt pair it had itself broadcast in the request, with receiptId only shape-checked (provider-delivery-protocol.ts requireReceiptId). Every one of those values is readable by any script in the same document, so a same-page script could resolve a pending signTransaction with attacker-chosen "signed" bytes or reject it with a fabricated terminal failure. The pre-existing tests WERE that forgery: every success in provider-page-request.test.ts was delivered through MockPage.emit({source: this, origin}) with a hardcoded receipt id, and the one wrong-context case covered a foreign source/origin but never a well-formed same-window forgery against a pending entry. The fix is a one-shot capability handshake over a transferred MessagePort, chosen over a minted nonce because a nonce is observable the moment anything logs or reflects it while a port cannot be named by later same-document script. DIRECTION, AND WHY IT CHANGED: 69a6282c7dea5e959e17e02dcc49c86ca5450898 pushed the grant unsolicited from the content owner's constructor; the real-Chromium lane refuted that (a document_start content script's window.postMessage is a queued task, so a main-world owner constructed later missed the grant entirely and could never settle -- 7 of 15 browser tests failed). 243f469d1f40d34922785acea2cd598614f10845 made it claim-then-grant: the page owner posts exactly one capability claim as it is constructed, the content owner answers only the first claim in a document and never mints a second channel. Whoever asks first gets the one port, so the owner the extension installs at document_start wins by construction. LIMITS, stated rather than implied. (1) THE PIPELINE IS UNSHIPPED. scripts/build.mjs keeps page/provider-request-owner.ts off BOTH bundles and content/provider-content-transport.ts off the content bundle, and the emitted content.js is byte-for-byte identical to the pre-X-1 bundle (verified by rebuilding at the parent of 69a6282c7dea5e959e17e02dcc49c86ca5450898 and comparing sha256), so nothing a user can reach exercises this. (2) The C1 bridge residual STANDS and is not narrowed: requests still travel over window.postMessage, so a same-page script can still observe, suppress, spoof, or replay the request half, and can still deny service entirely. Only SETTLEMENT is capability-bound. (3) SUPERSEDED BY WRDF-0121: a hostile script that posts the first structurally valid capability grant does not merely suppress the real grant; ProviderPageRequestOwner accepts the attacker-controlled port, and a terminal envelope on it can settle the promise. (4) ORDERING IS A PRECONDITION, NOT A PROOF: the main-world owner must be installed by the extension's own document_start injection so that its claim is the first in the document. No production entry point constructs this owner yet, so nothing enforces that ordering today. WRDF-0121 is CONFIRMED by static trace and adopted, but remediation is blocked on owner decision O8; it must bind the accepted port to extension-owned bootstrap state, which does not exist until that architecture is chosen and shipped. The invariant is therefore knocked down to unimplemented, not left test-covered by tests that only distinguish window delivery from delivery on an arbitrary first port. (5) BROWSER EVIDENCE EXISTS BUT IS NARROW. The Playwright lane now drives the real handshake between a document_start ISOLATED content script and a MAIN-world page script, which is the first real-Chromium evidence that the cross-world MessagePort transfer this design rests on actually works; bfcache, prerender, and same-document navigation behaviour of the transferred port are NOT measured. (6) The onReceiptPosted option added in 243f469d1f40d34922785acea2cd598614f10845 is observation-only: it exists because the receipt no longer crosses window where the browser fixture used to watch it, it carries nothing the capability holder does not already have, and a throwing observer cannot change settlement. (7) WRD-EXT-01/02 stay unimplemented for their own reasons; this row certifies only the settlement authenticity rule.

title: Approval-path capacity is shared per origin beneath every global cap
statement: Each approval-path pool enforces a per-origin share beneath its global cap — at most one open approval window per (origin, documentId) and four per origin, four signed-result flows per origin, four preparing-or-active approval requests per origin, and sixteen retained journal rows per origin — so one origin saturating its share never denies another origin its own full share; the global cap is evaluated first and still refuses with its own error, an origin-scoped refusal is a distinguishable error carrying only the refused site's browser-authenticated origin, and worker-restart invalidation deletes retention-expired journal rows during the walk it already performs.

evidence.name: gives each origin and document a share beneath the global window cap
still enforces the global window cap across many origins
keeps serving a second origin after the first has used its whole share
refuses a lease that presents no browser-derived origin
serves a second origin after the first has used its whole share
refuses one origin's excess with a distinguishable origin-scoped error
serves a second origin while the first has exhausted its share
reports global exhaustion as global exhaustion, ahead of the origin share
frees a terminal row only once its retention window has fully elapsed

notes: Seeded and landed together by audit finding X-2 (Low, gated) in commit 69a6282c7dea5e959e17e02dcc49c86ca5450898. X-2: the four approval-path pools were flat global counters — 16 windows (approval-window.ts), 32 signed-result flows, 32 preparing-or-active approval requests, 128 journal rows — with no per-origin subdivision and no test in which two origins competed, so one hostile http(s) origin could hold all of any of them. The journal was the worst case: a failed row is swept only on a later successful claim(), and only after PROVIDER_OPERATION_RETENTION_MS (10 minutes), so every other origin saw ProviderOperationCapacityError for the whole retention window after the attack stopped. LIMITS, stated rather than implied. (1) THE PIPELINE IS UNSHIPPED for three of the four pools: scripts/build.mjs keeps provider-signed-result-flow.ts, provider-approval-request.ts and provider-operation-store.ts off the background bundle. approval-window.ts IS in the shipped background bundle, but nothing shipped can reach launch() with a scope because the provider route that supplies one is itself gated. The status is test-covered because the tests are real, NOT because a shipped path runs them. (2) THE NUMBERS ARE POLICY, NOT MEASUREMENT. 1 window per document, 4 windows per origin, 4 flows per origin, 4 approval requests per origin, 16 journal rows per origin were chosen so no origin holds more than a quarter of any global pool and so one document can never hold two simultaneous modal approvals. No load, abuse, or real-usage data stands behind them; they are exported owner-tunable constants in provider-origin-capacity.ts. (3) THE QUOTA SUBJECT IS (origin, documentId) AS CHROME REPORTED IT. An attacker controlling many origins or many subdomains still scales linearly, and four cooperating origins can still exhaust any global pool. This bounds a single-origin denial of service; it is not a general anti-abuse control. (4) THE WINDOW QUOTA IS OPTIONAL AT THE API. ApprovalWindowLauncher.launch takes the scope as a third argument; the provider route always passes it, derived from owned.provenance and never from anything the page restates, but a route with no page principal (privileged UI, browser-worker harnesses) passes none and is bounded only by the global cap. Refusing an unscoped launch outright would break routes that legitimately have no page origin, so an unscoped launch is deliberately unattributable. (5) F-10 IS ONLY PARTLY DONE. Worker-restart invalidation (invalidatePreparing) now deletes retention-expired rows during the full cursor walk it already performs. The read() and database-open sweeps were NOT done: read() is a single-key point lookup on the replay hot path and cursorising it is a real behavioural change, and openProviderOperationDatabase performs no data access and has no injected clock. (6) THE JOURNAL EVIDENCE IS UNIT-LEVEL, NOT IndexedDB-LEVEL. provider-operation-store.ts still has no vitest harness; its admission and retention decisions were extracted into pure exported functions and tested directly, and its only end-to-end coverage remains the Playwright browser lane. (7) ProviderOperationOriginCapacityError cannot extend the shared ProviderOriginCapacityError because the store's hierarchy is rooted in ProviderOperationStoreError; it carries the same providerOriginCapacity marker, still extends ProviderOperationCapacityError so existing handlers keep working, and isProviderOriginCapacityRefusal recognises both.

title: Local decode of signed bytes; no blind-sign in v1
statement: Supported instructions are decoded locally from serialized bytes; unknown or ambiguous instructions never receive a benign verdict and there is no blind-sign fallback in v1.

Remaining acceptance: a merged-SHA test carrying the recorded assertion through assertionToCompact → a production secp256r1-precompile transaction builder → LiteSVM with_mainnet_features(), raw-high-S REJECT + normalized ACCEPT — lands alongside/after C3. title: Release producer git children are pinned and environment-isolated
statement: Every git child spawned by the release producer runs the absolute /usr/bin/git under an allow-listed environment, so neither a `git` executable earlier on the inherited PATH nor an inherited GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_INDEX_FILE/GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES/GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY can change the clean-tree verdict or the source.gitCommit recorded in the artifact manifest.

evidence.name: uses an absolute git path and ignores a git shim placed first on PATH
ignores an inherited GIT_DIR pointing at a different repository

notes: Audit finding E-1 (Medium). Before a4c134e83eb02554bda688917b97c554ce96bfbf the producer's run() was execFile("git", args, {cwd, encoding, maxBuffer}) with no env and no timeout; pnpm run prepends node_modules/.bin to PATH, so a dependency shipping a `git` bin shadowed the real executable for the clean-tree gate and for the rev-parse HEAD that becomes source.gitCommit, the value release-source-tag.mjs string-compares against the signed tag's commit. The two cited tests are RED at the pre-fix behaviour: the shim ran, and an inherited GIT_DIR made rev-parse HEAD return the decoy repository's commit. A third test in the same file is a drift guard asserting no producer script (package-release.mjs, release-artifact.mjs, local-dual-extension-release.mjs) spawns a bare `git` again, and a fourth pins the timeout/SIGKILL bound. LIMITS: this is environment pinning, not host attestation — it does not attest the bytes of /usr/bin/git, and says nothing about root or a malicious same-UID process. It is also git-only: the producer's `pnpm --version` child and the verifiers' `unzip` children still resolve through an inherited PATH, which is out of this row's scope.

title: CI release verification is anchored to committed owner pins, not co-generation
statement: A tagged release is verified in CI by the anchored verifiers (verify-release-source-tag.mjs, plus verify-reviewed-artifact-signature.mjs and verify-store-package.mjs when their tuples are pinned) against expectations read from a committed owner-authored apps/extension/release-pins.json — expected tag object SHA, primary and signing OpenPGP fingerprints, artifact-manifest SHA-256, and, when present, the dual-report, artifact-review-signature, and store-package/extension-id tuples. The pins loader fails CLOSED on a missing, unparsable, placeholder, incomplete, unknown-keyed, or malformed pins file, and on optional tiers that skip a level of the source-tag verifier's nested grammar; absent optional tuples are skipped with an explicit notice naming what is therefore not bound. Verifier children are spawned with an explicit argv (never a shell string) under the release-git.mjs environment allow-list plus an absolute GNUPGHOME. The committed pins file is a deliberate placeholder, so the release-verify job is red until the owner supplies real pins; CI can only prove agreement with the pins AS COMMITTED, so it does not replace the owner's own out-of-repository verification.

evidence.name: REJECTS the placeholder pins file committed to the repository
rejects every placeholder token in every scalar field
refuses a store-package tuple without the review-signature tuple
composes the store tuple into a sixteen-operand source-tag call and runs the store verifier
is an allow-list that drops injected variables and carries GNUPGHOME
WRDF-0132 reaches the action audit in a clean checkout without node_modules

notes: Audit finding E-4 (Medium, process). Before this row the ONLY release check in CI was `pnpm --filter @warden/extension release:gate` (.github/workflows/ci.yml) = release:package && release:verify, which compares a ZIP against an .artifact.json the same job generated seconds earlier — a self-consistency check anchored to nothing. grep for the three anchored verifiers in .github/ returned zero hits, and no expected fingerprint, tag object SHA, artifact-manifest digest or extension id was committed anywhere in the repository; RELEASE-INTEGRITY.md already stated the co-generation weakness without acting on it. The cited tests are RED before 583f9ec: apps/extension/scripts/release-pins.mjs did not exist, so the test file failed at import. TWO OWNER DECISIONS ARE OPEN. (1) The release-verify trigger pattern is `v*`, a choice made at authoring — no release-tag naming convention is pinned anywhere in the repo (release-source-tag.mjs pins the annotated tag's MESSAGE grammar, not its name); narrow it if real tags differ. A wide pattern is safe because the runner refuses any tag that is not the pinned one. (2) Only the source-tag tier is mandatory; the dual-report, artifact-review-signature and store-CRX tuples are optional and are SKIPPED WITH A LOUD NOTICE when null — the owner must decide which become mandatory before a real release. The committed release-pins.json is a deliberate placeholder and the release-verify job therefore FAILS on every tag until the owner replaces it and commits the ASCII-armored release public key(s) under apps/extension/release-pubkeys/; a test asserts that rejection so the placeholder cannot quietly become acceptable. WRDF-0132 was CONFIRMED at 3fffa9ed7f48cd534d8c2a4809bee7a6da0cdff9 because this first-post-checkout audit imported an unavailable package and failed before validation. Commit 5b90231aee1632ee143d4e4cf81c8d8b2248f068 makes that audit dependency-free and fail-closed; its clean-checkout fixture and the combined action/license evidence suite passed 7/7 at that exact SHA. LIMITS (also in RELEASE-INTEGRITY.md 'CI release-verify job (anchored pins)'): no host attestation; no defence against a compromised GitHub runner, a replaced /usr/bin/git or /usr/bin/gpg on it, or a malicious pinned action; one builder on one host, so WRD-REL-01/02/03 are NOT promoted; and the pins live in the same repository the tag comes from, so an attacker who can push both can move both — the owner must ALSO run these verifiers locally from a keyring and pins record held outside this repository.
